data.narrative:
Lightelligence is a public-stage semiconductor company founded by Shen Yichen, Marin Soljaćić, Huaiyu Meng, and Spencer Powers, having raised $310M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 4 same-sector, same-stage public companies in Chips & Semiconductors, spanning Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B).

The peer-median method is the primary applicable framework. The 4-company cohort yields a median valuation of $19.0B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $39.2B. This wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in the public semiconductor peer set—likely driven by differences in commercialization stage, addressable market size, and path to profitability. A public-comp anchoring approach using sector P/S multiples (18.4x median across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue for the private target.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $16.2B to $21.9B, centered on the peer median of $19.0B. This range reflects peer-derived guidance only; material uncertainties remain around Lightelligence's revenue scale, gross margins, capital efficiency relative to public peers, and market adoption trajectory for its core optical computing architecture. The width of the peer range itself ($1.1B–$39.2B) signals that stage-and-sector matching alone provides limited precision in early-revenue or pre-revenue semiconductor ventures.
